audits.summary: The remote has 455 branch heads (confirmed with git ls-remote): 185 are merged and 270 are not. The branch list itself is not the main problem. The cost is that durable records live only on unmerged branches, so main is not the full record. Six classes of record are missing from main. (1) Results from jobs that ran on the live game. main's state/run_queue.json stops at job 632, but claude/project-thread-* branches hold the manifests, results bundles and queue rows for jobs 640-698, plus a results bundle for live quest deletes on 2026-11-07. (2) About 66 director ruling entries, 12 of which reuse an id that main has given to a different ruling. (3) 112 review files from 73 chatgpt/review-* branches. main has the matching *_HANDOFF.md files but not the review verdicts. (4) A Forge bug fix: the @jutsu reference fix in AI rules is still missing from main's runner. (5) The Duelyst redesign of the art skill. (6) The 58 MB Skyglass/Mother of Echoes sim harness. Push numbers and ruling ids are handed out on separate branches, so they already collide. The 2026-11-08 prune record lists 152 deleted branches, and all 152 still exist. delete_branch_on_merge is false. Every branch was force-updated in the 2026-11-09 history rewrite, so ancestry checks are reliable; 200 of the 270 unmerged branches were last touched before that date. Classification: 17 are already on main (A), 215 are superseded or abandoned (B; 70 of those are review-only branches to harvest first), and 38 are live work that needs an owner decision (C). The per-branch table is in notes/branches.md. Recommended order: harvest the live-run records and rulings to main first, then the review files. Next, bulk-delete the merged branches and the class A and duplicate-chain branches, and tag-archive the rest of class B. Finally, adopt a lifecycle rule (records and reviews land on main, numbers are reserved on main, auto-delete on merge, a TTL report) so the build-up does not return.

audits.area: Lane A code & CI (forge, player, harness, root builder files, guide-studio, scripts, tools, ops, .github)
audits.summary: The local code is healthier than CI shows. Everything I could run locally passed: player 675/675 tests, the dauntless planner suite 46/46 in pytest, all 9 scripts/test_*.py files (183 tests), the forge import, boundary, release-pin and budget checks, and the doctrine, packs, rulings and no-real-name gates. Forge CI on main, though, has been red for every run since the 2026-11-09 history rewrite. The forge tests hard-code commit SHAs from before the rewrite (art blobs at 10fb257, imagePack a84807a), and because `npm test` fails first, the bundle-reproducibility, fixtures and budget steps have not run on main for 18 days. A green fix already exists (PR #123, fable/ci-repair-20261114). It has been open since 11-14 and now has merge conflicts with main in two files. The biggest maintenance cost is noise on main: run-lock heartbeats (50-67 commits a day), hourly jutsu-engine log commits, daily sentinel drift commits, and three CI workflows that run on every one of those pushes. Bot workflows also commit onto fable/* and chatgpt/* branches, which breaks the one-writer rule for branches. The sentinel has recorded upstream contract drift every day for a month (removals included) and none of it has been adopted. One governance gap stands out: Forge source on an unmerged, red-CI branch (claude/project-thread-bxzz52, livePatch zeroInstantResidual) was used for live jobs 640/641 on 11-18, and main has no record of it. The validate.py --parity TypeError still reproduces, and every current Forge bundle triggers it, because Forge always writes checks:null. Lower-value cleanup: an unused relay.yml, five Ghost Ship harness copies, a stalled guide-studio, job-specific readback scripts, and 11k lines of planner/pilot code sitting under state/. Top moves, in order: rebase and merge PR #123; move operational state (lock, jutsu log, fights) to a dedicated branch; restrict bot commits to main; add one test workflow for the suites that never run in CI.

audits.summary: The orientation layer is broken in a structural way, not only out of date. The main problem is that live content work moved onto branches that never merge. Since about 11-16, live jobs have run from unmerged claude/project-thread-* branches: Stolen Stores/Isonade (hlg3nc, +101 commits, 40 bundles), the genin dungeon, Nettle Nova, rc335 and the residual-modifier fix. Run-lock claims on main name roughly 30 job numbers that have no manifest on main, and push numbers 627/631/632/640/641 collide. So main's run_queue, harvests and answers do not describe the live game. run_queue.json itself is about 45% wrong among its 21 non-done rows. 469-test, 510, 538, 545, 548, 549, 550, 593 and 597 all ran (results bundles prove it). There are duplicate ids (596, 597). One commit (4914fcb0) said "549/550 done" but its queue edit was lost. About 40 jobs that ran have no row at all. active-context/digest (11-08) is wrong in at least 10 places. For example it says Mother of Echoes is still hidden, but 597 released it on 11-14 (DONE success). The mechanism is the root cause: the digest is written by hand and session_open even edits it. It has gone stale twice, about 3 weeks each time. The time-sensitive item is the Watch Log Fourth Page (job 520). Its precondition has been met since 11-14, the schedule still says unpublished, and the weekly release is tonight (Fri 11-27, 6 PM CT). The director has to decide. Other findings: answers/ has been frozen since 08-30 data, so validate.py's name-collision lint is blind to all Skyglass, MoE and Gobblefather names. One Perfect Crop's workstream has said BLOCKED for two months after its launch manifest actually ran. push/ holds 214 manifests that ran fine, against its own README rule. state/ holds about 60 spent event and brief files. The top moves are: (1) a Lane B rule that live-content branches land on main, with push numbers reserved on main; (2) a run_queue validator plus reconciliation; (3) generate active-context from the queue, bundles, branches, CI and rulings instead of writing it by hand; (4) a staged archive pass using the map in the notes. Moving run-lock churn off main would also help: it is 57% of commits on main, and each one fires 3 CI workflows.

findings.title: Build the offload manifest and fetch/check tool before moving anything
findings.evidence: No external-asset mechanism exists today. Grep for R2, cloudflare, uploadthing and releases/download in scripts/, skills/ and forge/ finds only design docs. jutsu_studio.py already enforces sha256 on raw bytes (lines 1225-1245, 1445, 1965), so hash-addressed provenance is an established pattern. Image formats barely compress, and 1,164 files would mean many tiny fetches.
findings.recommendation: Add scripts/assets.py and assets/offloaded.jsonl, one sorted line per file: {"path","sha256","bytes","category":"M1..M5","store":"gh-release:<tag>" or "r2:<bucket>","pack":"<tar name>","added"}. Subcommands: `offload <glob>` hashes files, builds an uncompressed tar per (category, top dir) (about 60 packs), uploads it, appends lines and runs git rm --cached. `fetch <glob|dir>` downloads, verifies each sha256 and restores paths. `check` (CI, socket-free) requires the manifest to be sorted and unique, no manifest path to be tracked, and every path to fall under a .gitignore glob. Add the offload globs to .gitignore so fetched files cannot be re-committed. Add an offline selftest. Run the offload as one Lane A PR per category so each can be reviewed against the move list. Before deleting anything from the tree, verify every pack's sha256 against the manifest and against a re-download.
findings.payoff: Makes the 911 MB move reversible and verifiable. A fetch becomes one command for any design session that needs old previews or raws.

Missing: compile (stub, SA-04), the harness (SA-03), the batched decision card (SA-06), go-card generation (SA-07) and closeout (SA-08). The repo has no .claude/settings.json or hooks (only .claude/agents/tnr-relay.md). Full flow diagram is in section 7 of the notes file.

(2) The design sheet runs through design.py check with the P2 libraries, then the freeze card. (3) For bosses and fights, designing-tnr-pve-encounters sets the shape and budget. (6) producing-tnr-art takes the art slots. (7) `design.py decisions` emits ONE decision card combining design, sim, reward, rarity and publish questions. A PreToolUse guard on TNR connector write procedures refuses without a held run-lock token, which reinforces the CLAUDE.md section 6 gates. findings.director_decision: Approve the three-touchpoint session shape (concept pick, one decision card, go). Also approve adding repo-level Claude Code hooks (SessionStart drift check, Stop closeout, PreToolUse run-lock guard on connector writes).

audits.area: Run lock and player telemetry off main
audits.summary: Since 2026-11-08, 1316 of the 2309 commits on origin/main touch only state/run_lock.json. About 300 more ("player: jutsu engine" and "jutsu training refill") rewrite only state/player/dauntless/jutsu_training.md, and more come from fight logs pushed by player/keep.py and from dauntless session/playbook commits. Over the last 8 days that is 85-90% of the 70-106 commits per day. The packed size is small (state/player 1.4 MB, run_lock.json 0.1 MB). The real costs are a history nobody can read, every main push competing with lock heartbeats, and three CI workflows with no branch or path filter running on every lock push. The lock code is easy to move. forge/tools/run_lock.mjs already reads RUN_LOCK_BRANCH, and player/keep.py already reads KEEP_BRANCH. The safety check (a write only succeeds against the version just read: a fast-forward push from the CLI, a blob-sha-checked contents-API PUT from the browser) works the same on any branch. Only the browser Forge has main hard-coded (forge/src/github.mjs GH.branch, used by readExact/writeExact). No raw.githubusercontent or release_pin reader touches the lock or the telemetry. I recommend option (a), but as two dedicated branches: ops/run-lock (only the lock file, so only real lock writers compete) and ops/player-log (append-only telemetry). Option (b), a ref outside branches, would force the browser onto the 4-call Git Data API, it is unverified that GitHub accepts such refs, and the director could not see it in the UI. Option (c), Issues/Gist, has no conditional write, so it loses the lock's safety. Cutover must be fail-closed: claim the main lock to block everyone, create ops/run-lock, merge the code, then leave a permanent 'held by moved' tombstone on main so old bundles and checkouts refuse instead of claiming. Never delete the main file, because old code reads a missing file as a free lock. RUL-2026-11-07-133 says in so many words that the lock is on main, so the director has to approve amending that ruling.

findings.title: Move the run lock to a dedicated branch ops/run-lock (recommended: option a)
findings.evidence: git log origin/main --since=2026-11-08 -- state/run_lock.json | wc -l = 1316 of 2309. Last 8 days: 11-21 105 commits/67 run-lock, 11-24 78/64, 11-27 74/53. forge/tools/run_lock.mjs:29-31 already has RUN_LOCK_REPO / RUN_LOCK_REMOTE / RUN_LOCK_BRANCH (default 'main'). Each write is one commit built in a private index and pushed as a plain fast-forward with 4 retries (lines 41-74). mcp_run.mjs:46 and player/runlock.py:45-74 both go through this tool, so one default change moves every CLI runner (Claude, player brain, jutsu engine, pvp, shipping skill). Options compared: (b) a ref outside refs/heads (e.g. refs/tnr/lock): the CLI push might work (not verified that GitHub accepts it), but the browser cannot write it with the contents API and would need blob+tree+commit+PATCH ref force=false (4 calls, a bigger bundle; not verified that the refs API accepts custom namespaces), and the GitHub UI does not show it. (c) Issues/Gist: the API has no conditional write, so two claimers could both win; this breaks the RUL-133 safety. An external store with conditional writes (D1/Durable Object) adds infrastructure and a second browser credential. Rejected.
findings.recommendation: Adopt option (a). Branch ops/run-lock is created as an orphan holding only state/run_lock.json. Code changes: run_lock.mjs BRANCH default becomes 'ops/run-lock'; if the branch is missing, the tool refuses (fail closed) instead of creating it. The browser Forge gets a lockBranch (RL-03). Tests keep using RUN_LOCK_REPO plus a branch override. Docs updated (RL-08). The safety check is unchanged: the CLI's fast-forward push on a branch with only lock commits is a check on the lock file itself, and the browser's blob-sha PUT works the same on any branch. Lane A work on a fable/* branch with ChatGPT review, since this is a mutation path that guards the live game.
findings.payoff: About 57% of main's commits since 11-08 leave main, so main's log is readable again. Lock heartbeats no longer compete with real work pushes (and the reverse), which removes a latent lost-lease and stopped-sends risk. Roughly 3 CI runs per lock write stop (RL-07).
findings.director_decision: Approve moving the run lock from main to a dedicated branch named ops/run-lock (RUL-2026-11-07-133 item 2 currently says 'state/run_lock.json on main'), recorded as a new ruling that amends 133?

findings.title: Keep the lock and the telemetry on separate branches; a shared ops branch would bring back the contention
findings.evidence: run_lock.mjs attempt() (lines 64-74): any push to the target branch between fetch and push makes the lock write fail its fast-forward check and retry, with at most 4 attempts, then 'could not push the lock'. player/runlock.py _renew(): if a heartbeat push fails, the lease simply runs out ('the push failed: the lease runs out by itself'), and sends stop at STOP_MARGIN. keep.py (lines 79-92) uses the same fast-forward push. If fight logs and the hourly jutsu log share a branch with the lock, every telemetry push competes with heartbeats. I found no recorded contention failure (grep for 'could not push the lock after' / 'non-fast-forward' in state/, docs/, player/ came back empty), so this is a design risk, not an observed incident.
findings.recommendation: Use two branches: ops/run-lock (written only by run_lock.mjs and the Forge lockStore) and ops/player-log (keep.py, the jutsu engine log, session logs). The only commits on the lock branch then come from real lock writers.
findings.payoff: The lock's renewal path only competes with other lock writers, so a heartbeat cannot fail because of an unrelated push.

findings.title: Browser Forge has main hard-coded for the lock; needs a lockBranch, a bundle rebuild and a userscript reload
findings.evidence: forge/src/github.mjs:7 GH = {branch: 'main', ...}. readExact (line 80) calls gh._url(path), which defaults ref to cfg.branch. writeExact (line 91) sends body.branch = gh.cfg.branch. forge/src/core/core.mjs:70-73 lockStore uses readExact/writeExact(LOCK_PATH). _url(path, ref) already accepts a ref, so the change is small. The bundle budget is checked (RUL-2026-11-07-134, forge/tools/check_bundle_budget.mjs). release_pin.yml re-pins on a forge_bundle.js push to main. Duet runs browser Forge for image jobs (RUL-2026-11-07-135). The results-bundle PUT to harvests/inbox (Github.put) must stay on main because answers.yml triggers on harvests/**.
findings.recommendation: Add GH.lockBranch = 'ops/run-lock'. readExact/writeExact get a branch argument, used only by core.mjs lockStore. Github.put and list keep main. Extend forge/test/github.cors.test.mjs and core tests to assert the lock calls use ?ref=ops/run-lock and body.branch=ops/run-lock, and that harvest PUTs still target main. Rebuild the bundle, run the budget check, let release_pin pin it, and ask the director/Duet to reload the userscript before step 5 of RL-04.
findings.payoff: The browser runner joins the same lock as the CLI runners. Without this, the move would split the lock in two and allow two writers on the account at once.

findings.title: Cutover must be fail-closed: tombstone main's lock, never delete it
findings.evidence: forge/src/runner/runlock.mjs parseLock: 'Missing or empty text is a free lock'. So if main's file were deleted, any old checkout or cached old bundle would claim on main while new code claims on ops: two writers, a mutation overrun, and the 1% money/bank fine in RUL-133. lockState() treats any token with a future expiresAt as held, and claimDecision refuses ('held by <holder> (<job>)'). parseLock places no upper bound on expiresAt. checkTtl caps tool claims at 240 min, so the tombstone needs a one-off checked commit (same commitLock path). Today's main lock (state/run_lock.json) is held by player, 'dauntless war pilot', until 2026-11-27T21:22Z, so the cutover must wait for a free lock.
findings.recommendation: Order: (1) wait for the lock to be free, then `run_lock.mjs claim --holder migration --job 'move lock to ops/run-lock' --ttl 240` on main, which proves it is free and blocks every old client. (2) Create orphan ops/run-lock whose run_lock.json is a release body (releasedAt=now, so the 65 s quiet period still applies). (3) Merge the RL-01/03 PR; release_pin re-pins; director reloads. (4) Use the migration token to replace main's lock with a permanent tombstone {holder:'moved', job:'run lock moved to ops/run-lock (RUL-...)', token, expiresAt:'2099-...'}. Old code then refuses with a readable reason. Rollback: revert the PR (or RUN_LOCK_BRANCH=main) and release the tombstone with its token, which is visible in the file. Ship this sequence as a scripted step (e.g. forge/tools/run_lock.mjs migrate) tested against local bare repos, like runlock.test.mjs, rather than as hand steps.
findings.payoff: There is no window in which two runners can each believe they hold the lock, and rollback is one revert plus one release.
findings.director_decision: Schedule the cutover window: all runners (player brain, jutsu engine schedule, Duet, browser Forge) idle for about 15 minutes while the lock moves; director go for that window.

findings.title: Fight logs: point keep.py at ops/player-log and decouple 'where fights are read' from 'rehearsal'
findings.evidence: player/keep.py:24-26 has KEEP_BRANCH (default main) and only accepts paths under state/player/<acct>/fights/ (line 46). combat.py:360-361 spawns `python -m player.keep BID` when C.keeps_fights(). player/config.py fights_dir() honours TNR_PLAYER_FIGHTS, but keeps_fights() returns False whenever TNR_PLAYER_FIGHTS or TNR_PLAYER_LIVE is set, because it treats that as a rehearsal. So redirecting the fights folder to an ops worktree would silently stop keeping fights. 79 files in fights/ (1.4 MB). .gitignore already excludes state/player/*/live/ and fights/live/.
